title: Cristóbal Mateo Argumedo to Félix Díaz, 5 and 20 October 1921 (catalogue 1445, CEHM-Carso DCXXI.3.244.1 and 3.250.2): the cipher runs Narváez did not print, read with his published table

steps.what: Four page images fetched with curl from the CEHM-Carso public viewer, no sign-in (path pattern from PR #941).
35 runs (all cipher pairs of the four folios) transcribed and frozen by SHA-256, with Narváez's key, before any decoding.
The 10 runs whose clear Narváez prints, decoded with his frozen table: 88 of 89 letters agree (0.989); the miss is the writer's PELIGRN, which Narváez corrects silently.
The 25 runs Narváez did not print read in their clear sentences: 32 words, 25 as the key gives them, 7 marked one-code slips or overstrikes, none supplied or unread. check_marks.py passes.

Write-up escalation (print): does Narváez's book Criptografía diplomática, política y militar en México (1813-1926) (SRE, 2019, 495 pp.) print these runs? Google Books (id 1CrBzgEACAAJ) shows 'Preview unavailable' and 'Search inside unavailable'; the gdata feed finds no text for Argumedo, Panindícuaro or Benítez/Heredia; books.google.* gave a CAPTCHA, and the SRE catalogue page a bot check. The Historia Mexicana review (G. Martínez Carmona, 72.2, pp. 963-966, via SciELO) says the chapters were published before (2007-2015) and modified for the book, and that pp. 370-371, 374-375, 378 and 382-383 were missing from the reviewer's printed copy; it does not name Argumedo. The book's Wellington section (pp. 364-369) prints the same runs as the 2015 article (wellington1922 NOTES). Whether the Argumedo pages of the book print more than 2015 could not be told.

Write-up escalation (siblings): the Amaya letter of catalogue 1445 (DCXXI.3.242.1, Havana, 27 Sep 1921, to Félix Díaz), the one other felicista letter noted with two-digit numbers, fetched from the CEHM-Carso viewer (images 0001-0002) and looked at: its pairs run to 79, 86, 90, 96 and 97, outside the 01-37 of Argumedo's table, so it is another table. The Mina letters use groups of numbers and letters (catalogue 1445 note). No other letter in this table and no second copy of Argumedo's two letters was found.

validation.notes: The table is Narváez's printed key, applied unchanged and not built from these letters; no null-key test was run. Control against his printed clear: 88 of 89 letters.

outcome.method_basis: Narváez's published table for these two letters (2015, p. 122), applied unchanged to the 25 runs he did not print in 2015; this completes his reading. His 2019 book could not be searched; if it prints these runs, the method for them would become read from existing decipherment.
outcome.fraction_read_source: All cipher words of the two letters: 50, of which 41 read as the key gives them and 9 marked (7 in the new runs, 2 in Narváez's controls). New runs alone: 25 of 32 (0.781).

credits.note: the system, the two-digit table and the clear of 10 runs of these two letters (not repeated as new here)
credits.source: R. Narváez, 'Sobre algunos criptosistemas mexicanos de principios del siglo XX', Documenta & Instrumenta 13 (2015), pp. 107-132, table at p. 122

texts.label: Argumedo to Félix Díaz, 5 Oct 1921: 26 cipher runs
texts.summary: A Michoacán landowner's son, Alfredo Gutiérrez, offers his father's hacienda and a guerrilla of 80-100 armed men and asks for a nombramiento to win over the peons of Panindícuaro; agents Gral. Benítez, Heredia, Mata, Montaño, Lic. Mena, Lic. P., Don Miguel; Obregón's government called the 'reigning horde' and the 'Agua Prieta mob'.
texts.note: Runs in bold in clear Spanish sentences. 38 cipher words: 31 read as the key gives them, 7 marked (one-code slips and an overstrike: AGUA, BENÍTEZ x2, H., ALFREDO, DÍAZ, FÉLIX), 0 supplied, 0 unread. New runs (21, not printed by Narváez): 27 words, 20 read.

reading_review.by: integration review of PR #962 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person
reading_review.note: Read both letters' runs in their sentences: continuous Spanish (the reigning horde, the Agua Prieta mob, Benítez, the Michoacán hacienda and guerrilla offered through Heredia, the nombramiento for Panindícuaro; granted with the rank of colonel on 20 Oct). Own decoder matches both decryption files; control 88 of 89 letters; recount 31/38 (3.244.1) and 10/12 (3.250.2, short-text floor). Runs compared with the CEHM images A01-A26 (A11 at full size) and B05-B09. Read in part.

texts.label: Argumedo to Félix Díaz, 20 Oct 1921: 9 cipher runs
texts.summary: The danger threatening the felicistas is laid at the door of 'Don Pancho and partners'; the document asked of Don Miguel for the man from Panindícuaro was granted with the rank of colonel.
texts.note: Read by the short-text floor (README, 19 Nov 2026): 12 cipher words, 10 read as the key gives them, 2 holes (PELIGR{N/O}, P{D/A}NCHO, both in Narváez's control runs). The new runs B05-B08: 5 words, 5 read.

reading_review.note: Read both letters' runs in their sentences: continuous Spanish (the reigning horde, the Agua Prieta mob, Benítez, the Michoacán hacienda and guerrilla offered through Heredia, the nombramiento for Panindícuaro; granted with the rank of colonel on 20 Oct). Own decoder matches both decryption files; control 88 of 89 letters; recount 31/38 (3.244.1) and 10/12 (3.250.2, short-text floor). Runs compared with the CEHM images A01-A26 (A11 at full size) and B05-B09. Read in part.

gaps.detail: The second pair is a 0 with 6 and 3 typed one over the other; 03 gives Agua Prieta, 06 no word.

gaps.item: six marked words of the new runs: BEN{E/I}TEZ x2, {H} before HEREDIA, {D/A}LFREDO, D{E/I}AZ, FELI{Z/X}
gaps.detail: The writer's signs are one code off (seen on the image) or, for {H}, of uncertain sense, so the key does not give the word as written; each is read by the sense. No second copy of either letter was found (siblings step, 25 Nov 2026), so no other witness can give them.

prior.where: Narváez 2015 pp. 117-122: system, table, and the clear of 10 runs of these two letters; he says the table reads the rest and prints none of it (3.244.1 cut with '[...]'; the four f. 2 runs of 3.250.2 in cipher only). His 2019 book could not be opened or searched (25 Nov 2026): whether it prints more of these letters is not known.

human: Brice Dudout chose the target and approved the submission; an AI model (Claude) transcribed, applied the published table, read and checked. No person has checked the transcription or the reading.
